nested_lists.name: entitlements
nested_lists.shape_reason: an LES lists ~5–15 entitlement lines (base pay, BAH, BAS, special/hazard pay), each a {label, amount} pair; flat rows are light and stay well under the 16,384-token ceiling

fields.name: label
fields.why: the entitlement line label (BAH, BAS, base pay, special/hazard pay); BAH/BAS are non-taxable and must be itemized so underwriting can gross them up. Capture the label verbatim; do not expand

fields.name: amount
fields.why: the entitlement amount; the income-calc input that separates taxable from non-taxable pay

rejected.name: form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: LES is a fixed DFAS format; no per-file version consumer

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: an LES is system-generated, not executed

rejected.name: remarks
rejected.reason: no consumer; catch-all captures LES remarks

encoding_variations: branch_or_component (enum, null): 'Army', 'USMC', 'Navy', 'Air Force', 'Space Force', 'Coast Guard'; and Active / Reserve / National Guard.
pay_period (date_range, no coercer): military LES often shows a single month; keep verbatim.
Entitlement labels are terse codes/abbreviations ('BAH', 'BAS', 'COLA', 'SDAP', 'HFP/IDP') — capture the label verbatim; do not expand.
pay_grade: 'E-5', 'O-3', 'W-2' (warrant) — the letter+number pair disambiguates enlisted/officer/warrant.

open_questions.q: One list or three. entitlements, deductions, allotments are three parallel object[]s.
options: a single combined pay_line_items flat list with a category column covering all three
open_questions.recommendation: (a) one entitlements list now — the sole income-calc consumer; escalate to (b) if a rule needs typed deductions/allotments

open_questions.q: Tax objects flattened to str. federal/fica/state_tax_data are objects degraded to strings.
open_questions.recommendation: keep flattened; if a withholding rule ever needs the components, they'd need sub-field promotion

open_questions.q: SSN field name. social_security_number_masked differs from the registry's taxpayer_ssn_masked.
open_questions.recommendation: confirm whether to reuse the existing key or register a new one

notes: No rules in the packet → no rule floor. The LES is the military analogue of a pay stub: its purpose is income qualification. The typed core captures the service member's identity, the pay period, the gross/net figures, and the entitlement detail (BAH/BAS are tax-advantaged and grossed up). Every field is justified by identity, PII, or processor review; a future income-calculation rule is the obvious consumer of the pay figures and the entitlements list.

The entitlements list is the one list that carries income-calc value (catalog mortgage_use: 'Calculate gross military income'), because BAH/BAS are non-taxable and get grossed up — the itemization separates taxable from non-taxable pay. Serves no rule today but is the highest-value future consumer. deductions and allotments are summarized by the total_deductions / total_allotments scalars.

social_security_number_masked — highly_restricted; needs _PII_FIELDS registration, pre_masked true. Not in the current 7-field registry (distinct name from taxpayer_ssn_masked) — flag. Unregistered ⇒ full SSN could land unmasked in the catch-all.
direct_deposit_account_last4 — restricted; needs _PII_FIELDS registration, pre_masked true. Flattened from the direct_deposit_institution_and_account_last4 object.
service_member_name — personal name, retained as typed identity (not a _PII_FIELDS entry).

Prompt hint (doc-level): BAH (housing) and BAS (subsistence) are non-taxable allowances — they must be itemized in entitlements, not merged into a single gross, because underwriting grosses them up. Money stays a string in value, coerced to Decimal on read.
